defs.def: to decide that sth that has been arranged will not now take place 取消；撤销；终止

ex.s: The organizers had to cancel the outdoor concert due to the sudden thunderstorm, _________ many eager fans who had been waiting for hours.
ex.t: 你还可以在阿姆斯特丹以外骑行欣赏美丽的风景。

ex.s: When enough of these errors are averaged together, they cancel each other out, resulting in a more accurate estimate.
ex.t: 当足够多的这类错误被平均在一起时，它们会相互抵消，从而得出更准确的估算。

ex.s: If people are similar and tend to make the same errors, then their errors won’t cancel each other out.
ex.t: 如果人们彼此相似并倾向于犯同样的错误，那么他们的错误就不会相互抵消。

ex.s: On which of the following dates can you cancel your registration with a full refund?
ex.t: 以下哪个日期你可以取消注册并获得全额退款？

ex.s: His father's flight was unexpectedly canceled, ____29____him to fly alone.

ex.s: The two sets of waves cancel each other out.
ex.t: 嗯，它的工作原理是分析传入声波并产生第二组传出声波。

ex.s: Refund Policy—the subscription can be canceled within 28 days and you can get your money back.

defs.def: to say that you no longer want to continue with an agreement, especially one that has been legally arranged 撤销，取消，废除（具有法律效力的协议）

ex.s: The stronger a reusable bag is, the longer its life and the more plastic-bag use it cancels out.
ex.t: 然而，耐用的可重复使用购物袋通常需要更多的能源来制造。

defs.def: to mark a ticket or stamp so that it cannot be used again 盖销，注销（票或邮票）
